title: Increase in and Safeguarding against Securities Trading Fueled by Online Discussions and Social Media Chat Groups
what_it_is: Increase in and Safeguarding against Securities Trading Fueled by Online Discussions and Social Media Chat Groups

sections.label: Online trading and market safeguards
sections.summary: No signs that online discussions significantly increased Singapore-listed securities trading, but MAS and SGX RegCo are on heightened alert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether there are signs of significant increase in securities trading fueled by online discussions and social media chat groups; (b) what are the protections against such activities destabilising the smooth running of the securities market; and (c) whether MAS is considering safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: There have been no signs that discussions in online forums or social media chat groups have led to any significant increase in the trading of securities listed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) are on heightened alert to such activities.

sections.label: Fallen prices and safeguards
sections.summary: Prices have fallen from their peaks, raising whether the increases were sustainable, and safeguards address such risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: These prices have since fallen from their peaks, raising a new issue of whether the price increases were sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We have various safeguards in place to address such risks.

sections.label: Three market safeguards
sections.summary: The safeguards are market transparency, curbing sharp price movements, and enforcing against market misconduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: One, providing market transparency; two, curbing any sharp price movements; and three, enforcing against market misconduct.

sections.label: Short positions in Singapore
sections.summary: Short positions in Singapore are much less compared to the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On short squeezes, the short positions in Singapore compared to the US, are much less.

sections.label: Transparency, US options, short squeezes
sections.summary: Transparency gives investors more information, and US single stock options add short positions causing short squeezes, which Singapore lacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, because of the transparency, investors have more information to act on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And thirdly, there are also mechanisms in the US such as having single stock options – you can have many puts, for example; it is equivalent to short selling – that also exposures themselves to more short positions, resulting in short squeezes; which we do not have here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, for various reasons, plus all the measures I mentioned earlier – enforcement, being alert to such price surges, implementing circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will continue to be on the alert to prevent such events, such short squeezes from happening.
